newsitem.title: UK: Major says Britain will not be sidelined by EMU.
newsitem.headline: Major says Britain will not be sidelined by EMU.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major denied on Tuesday that Britain would be sidelined at international economic summits if it did not join a single European currency.
Major told the Conservatives' last election rally before the May 1 election that London was one of the major financial centres in the world and Britain would have a say in world economic policy.

Responding to suggestions by European commissioner for monetary union Yves Thibault de Silguy that a G3 summit consisting of America, Japan and the European Union would replace the G7 summits of the world's major economic nations, Major said it was "absurd and arrogant".
"Today a European commissioner has suggested that if Britain doesn't join the single currency we would be marginalised in world discussions," Major said.

"London is one of the financial centres of the world, and will stay that way. The suggestion that the European Union would take over all representation on economic policy for members of the single currency is just the kind of danger I have been warning about.
"I would never accept that," he added.
Major has always insisted that Britain should adopt a "wait and see" policy about joining a single European currency.
